query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A minor compositional addition—specifically, the introduction of a small amount of boron (e.g., 0.5 at.%)—to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will refine the lamellar microstructure and promote formation of fine, thermally stable boride precipitates, thereby enhancing its strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance under extreme service conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with performance below industrial application requirements for fasteners.
generation.intervention: Add a minor composition change by doping the alloy with approximately 0.5 at.% boron.
generation.conditions: Operating as fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Refined lamellar microstructure with dispersed, fine boride precipitates at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Boron doping is expected to modify the solidification behavior, leading to a refined microstructure. The boride precipitates can pin dislocations and grain boundaries, improving load transfer and inhibiting creep deformation. Additionally, a more coherent and stabilized microstructure may reduce pathways for corrosive attack and improve resistance to thermal cycling.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the starting alloy, the boron-doped alloy should exhibit a measurable increase in strength and ductility (e.g., modest improvements on the order of ~10-20%), along with enhanced resistance to room-temperature creep and corrosion. The improvements are anticipated under the same service and test boundaries specified for fasteners.
generation.baseline: Performance metrics (mechanical strength, ductility, creep rate, and corrosion resistance) of the undoped, uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective specifically within the operational envelope of fasteners under extreme temperature fluctuations, sustained mechanical loads, room-temperature creep conditions, and moderate to severe corrosive environments. The addition level should remain within a narrow range (around 0.25–1 at.%) to avoid adverse microstructural changes.
generation.uncertainty: While prior studies on similar alloys suggest that minor boron additions can refine microstructures and improve mechanical properties, the exact magnitude of improvement and long-term stability under cyclic extreme conditions remain uncertain without targeted experimentation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one set of standard AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and another set with 0.5 at.% boron added. Subject both sets to a battery of tests including tensile testing, creep testing at room temperature, standardized corrosion testing in a simulated saline environment, and thermal cycling to replicate extreme temperature fluctuations.
measurements: Creep rate under constant loading at room temperature
Corrosion rate (e.g., weight loss or electrochemical measurements)
Fatigue life under thermal cycling conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped samples do not show a statistically significant improvement (i.e., at least a ~10% enhancement in performance metrics) over the undoped alloy across the tested properties, then the hypothesis that boron addition improves the overall performance for fastener applications is falsified.
